Topics · Is there a God?

Isn't the burden of proof on whoever claims?

Yes, the claimant bears it, and this text asks proof of all. 'I am not persuaded' carries none. What is fair?

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَقَالُوا۟ لَن يَدْخُلَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَن كَانَ هُودًا أَوْ نَصَـٰرَىٰ ۗ تِلْكَ أَمَانِيُّهُمْ ۗ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَـٰنَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." That is [merely] their wishful thinking. Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:111

Translation

Don’t trust in lying words, saying, ‘Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, are these.’

Original · Hebrew

אַל־תִּבְטְח֣וּ לָכֶ֔ם אֶל־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַשֶּׁ֖קֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה הֵֽמָּה׃

Jeremiah · 7:4

World English Bible

You are right. Whoever makes a claim carries the burden. If someone says a teapot orbits the sun, you owe no disproof. So this app does not ask you to disprove God, and it would be unfair if it did. This verse takes your side against a religious claim. A group says that only its own will be saved. The reply is short: produce your proof, if you are truthful. The rule binds this app as well.

A question for you

Which of these is closest to your own position?

If you sayI claim nothing. I am simply not persuaded.
ThenThen you carry no burden, and you will not be told otherwise here. What remains is whether you want to look at what is offered.
If you sayI claim there is no God.
ThenThat is a claim, and it bears as much as the opposite one does. That is fine, and you may well have reasons to offer.
If you sayI don't know, and I don't think anyone can.
ThenThe first half carries no burden. The second is a claim about the limits of knowledge, and it can be examined.

Part 2 of 3

﴿قُلْ أَرَءَيْتُم مَّا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَرُونِى مَاذَا خَلَقُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ ۖ ٱئْتُونِى بِكِتَـٰبٍ مِّن قَبْلِ هَـٰذَآ أَوْ أَثَـٰرَةٍ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, [O Muḥammad], "Have you considered that which you invoke besides Allāh? Show me what they have created of the earth; or did they have partnership in [creation of] the heavens? Bring me a scripture [revealed] before this or a [remaining] trace of knowledge, if you should be truthful."

Quran · Al-Ahqaf 46:4

So why is God not simply a bigger teapot? Because a teapot does no work. Nothing depends on it, nothing is explained by it, and removing it changes nothing. The claim about God offers an account: of why anything exists, why the world is ordered enough to understand, why anyone is able to ask. That does not make it true. It makes it a claim that can be argued about, and any rival account of the same things has to offer its reasons too. This verse asks for reasons too.

A question for you

Is the claim of a Source of the world like the teapot claim?

If you sayYes. Neither can be tested.
ThenThat is the strongest thing to say. The difference offered is that the first tries to explain something. You decide if that difference is enough.
If you sayNo. The first tries to explain the world.
ThenThen it deserves discussion, though it has not yet been shown. The burden of showing it still falls on it.
If you sayI don't think the world needs explaining.
ThenThat is a serious position, held in philosophy: the universe is simply there. It has its own question.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ ۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ ۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْـًٔا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they have thereof no knowledge. They follow not except assumption, and indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all.

Quran · An-Najm 53:28

So what standard is fair? It has to apply to both sides. 'Extraordinary claims need extraordinary evidence' is sound, but what counts as extraordinary depends on where you begin: a Source is extraordinary to one person, a universe with no Source to another. A claim that hides from every test is empty, so believers owe you tests their claims could fail. And guessing is not knowing, on any side. That last line is this verse, and it was first aimed at religious claims.

A question for you

Which standard are you willing to apply to both sides?

If you sayOnly what can be tested by experiment counts.
ThenCan that rule itself be tested by experiment? It is worth asking before you adopt it.
If you sayThe best explanation of everything we know.
ThenThat is the standard science, history and courts work by. Many Steps here rest on it, and you may reject their results.
If you sayI believe only what is beyond all doubt.
ThenVery little survives that standard, on either side. Suspending judgment is a fair position if it is applied evenly.

The same in the other books

Translation

“Come now, and let’s reason together,” says Yahweh: “Though your sins are as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool. If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good of the land; but if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured with the sword; for Yahweh’s mouth has spoken it.”

Original · Hebrew

לְכוּ־נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אִם־יִֽהְי֨וּ חֲטָאֵיכֶ֤ם כַּשָּׁנִים֙ כַּשֶּׁ֣לֶג יַלְבִּ֔ינוּ אִם־יַאְדִּ֥ימוּ כַתּוֹלָ֖ע כַּצֶּ֥מֶר יִהְיֽוּ׃ אִם־תֹּאב֖וּ וּשְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם ט֥וּב הָאָ֖רֶץ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃ וְאִם־תְּמָאֲנ֖וּ וּמְרִיתֶ֑ם חֶ֣רֶב תְּאֻכְּל֔וּ כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃

Isaiah · 1:18-20

World English Bible
